item.title: Unpacking the 2026 Midterm Elections — Wed Nov 4, 12:00 PM — Sanford 223
Is There a Capstone Phase for Your Faculty Career? — Wed Nov 4, 12:20 PM — Webcast
item.description:
A "capstone" is generally defined as a culmination or crowning achievement, and it can also be useful for helping faculty think about their careers and legacy. This conversation is for later-stage faculty who are not yet ready to retire but who seek to maximize their sense of meaning, purpose and impact within the next two, five or even ten years. Emeriti faculty panelists will discuss how they approached their "capstone" phase, and share advice for participants based on their experiences. What would a capstone phase look like for your faculty career, and how might you be intentional about planning one?
Source: Duke University

item.title: Biomimicry: Nature as a Mentor — Tue Nov 17, 1:00 PM — Swift Creek Bluffs Nature Preserve
item.description:
Learn about biomimicry at Swift Creek Bluffs! Biomimicry (from the Greek bios, meaning life, and mimesis, meaning to imitate) is the practice of looking at how plants, animals, and ecosystems solve problems and then copying those designs to solve human challenges. It’s not about using nature as a resource (like cutting down trees for wood); it’s about learning from nature as a mentor.
Join Hike Leader, Leigh Aultman, for an afternoon of Biological Storytelling. We will walk the short creek loop trail with up to six stops where stories will be shared about local organisms' biological adaptations and how those adaptations and innovations can inform human designs. This is a free event, but preregistration is required. Due to the size of the parking lot, we will keep the hiking group small and ask that you register by vehicle rather than individual. Feel free to bring guests but please carpool to ensure we have enough space in the parking lot.
Source: Triangle Land Conservancy

In under 90 minutes, you'll build a real, working AI agent, from scratch, no coding required, that reads every email, sorts it into categories, and tells you exactly what needs your attention first.
Every morning. Automatically. Done. Not a demo, not a concept, a live agent you build yourself and take home today. This is what it means to become Fluid-Shaped™: instead of doing everything yourself, you learn to summon exactly the help you need, the moment you need it. Think of it as hiring your first AI employee, then meeting the rest of the team you could hire/build next: an AI Chief of Staff and a bench of specialized advisors for Growth, Sales, Product, and Strategy. item.title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math — Mon Feb 1
item.description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.
Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. item.title: Building Blocks for MCP Servers — Tue Nov 3, 1:00 PM — The TEC - Technology Engagement Center
item.description:
In this hands-on, beginner-friendly 2-hour workshop, you'll build and deploy your first Model Context Protocol (MCP)server-the open-source standard that lets AI assistants securely connect to external data sources and tools across different platforms. Through a series of guided exercises, you'll create a custom MCP server from scratch, learn the core concepts of resources, tools, and prompts, and integrate your server with a range of AI clients-including ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and a deployed MyGPTBuilder instance. Whether you want to give AI applications live data access, build cross-platform tooling, or explore the emerging ecosystem of AI interoperability, you'll leave with the foundational knowledge and practical skills to start building with MCP. Familiarity with basic Python (or any object-oriented language) is encouraged before attending.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Chemistry Defense: Daniel Duan: "Multi-State Mechanocatalysis: Modulating Transition Metal Reactivity with Force" — Tue Nov 3, 1:30 PM — None
item.description:
Multi-State Mechanocatalysis: Modulating Transition Metal Reactivity with Force
Mechanical force has been associated with material destruction historically, most often through homolytic bond scission. More recently, force has been utilized constructively to alter polymer topology, trigger chemical reactions, and tune material properties. In this dissertation, we develop multi-state mechanocatalysis: a new class of polymer-embedded catalysts that funnel mechanical force to the molecular level to bias transition-metal catalysis. Unlike conventional on/off switchable catalysts, force is directional, continuous, and reversible, allowing catalytic rate and stereochemical outcome to be tuned across multiple force states.

item.title: Film Screening: "Zone of Interest" — Tue Nov 3, 7:00 PM — Rubenstein Arts Center
item.description:
The Jewish Studies Course 175CNS "Holocaust Memory through the Ages: Memoirs, Memorials, Movies" screens the film "The Zone of Interest."
The Zone of Interest (2023) Directed by Jonathan Glazer | Germany/United Kingdom/Poland | 105 min
Loosely based on Martin Amis's novel, The Zone of Interest offers a chilling and unconventional portrayal of the Holocaust by focusing not on the victims, but on the family of Rudolf Höss, the commandant of Auschwitz. Rudolf, his wife Hedwig, and their children live an idyllic life in a comfortable home directly beside the camp, tending a garden, raising a family, and enjoying the routines of domestic life while mass murder unfolds just beyond their garden wall.
